summary: Minimal, idiomatic fix replacing truthiness test of `im(a)` with fuzzy `im(a).is_zero is False`, correctly preventing the false-positive ValueError when `im` stays unevaluated under `evaluate(False)` while still rejecting genuinely imaginary coordinates. Aligns with SymPy's standard three-valued assumption idiom and is the correct, mergeable resolution.

issues.description: Semantics shift on the unknown case: when `im(a).is_zero` returns None (indeterminate) for a number, the old code raised but the new code permits the coordinate. For actual numbers (`is_number` guard) the imaginary part is normally decidable, so this is a corner case, but it slightly relaxes the rejection to only definitely-imaginary values.
